result:
12 of the 150 rules in `pricebook.py` didn't match their docstrings, and I fixed all of them. I built a reference version of each rule from its docstring and the module's shared rules, then compared all 150 rules against it across about 400 quantities × 12 unit prices. The mismatches are now 0 of 150.

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 08 | Discount rate was 13% | 12% |
| 17 | Discount started at 51 units | Starts at 50 units |
| 61, 62, 138 | The cap was applied to the price, then the rate was applied (`min(base, cap) * pct`) | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 82 | Used `round()` | Rounds down to the won (`// 100`) |
| 89 | Discount rate was 9% | 8% |
| 94, 118 | `qty > 20` left out exactly 20 units | `qty >= 20` |
| 99 | A whole rule was calculated as marginal (`(qty - 50) * unit`) | Calculated on the full amount (`base * 2 // 100`) |
| 108 | The cap was applied to the marginal amount, not the discount | Calculate the discount first, then cap the discount |
| 122 | Discount started at 101 units | Starts at 100 units |

Some rules are written differently but give the same results, such as `not qty < 5`, `50 <= qty`, an `if` used instead of `min`, and `(qty * unit)`. I left those as they were. I didn't touch any other code.

There are no tests in the project, so this comparison script is the only check. Because these are price rules, quotes from the 12 changed rules will now differ from the old ones.

STATUS: DONE
